items.title: PSK2a is required for cambial development and xylem formation during secondary growth in poplar.
items.abstract: Phytosulfokines (PSKs) are sulfated peptide hormones involved in plant growth, development, and stress responses. However, direct genetic evidence for the involvement of PSK peptide in cambium development and secondary vascular development in woody plants remains largely lacking. Here, we identified nine PSK family members in Populus trichocarpa. Phylogenetic, gene structure, conserved motif, and local synteny analyses indicated that the poplar PSK family is evolutionarily conserved, and some members may have arisen from the whole-genome duplication (WGD) event. PSK2a is one of several PSK family genes that are highly expressed in poplar stem vascular tissues, but shows low expression in roots. Subsequently, we generated PtrPSK2a (cloned from P. trichocarpa) overexpression lines in hybrid poplar 717 and CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout lines targeting its endogenous orthologs PtaPSK2a_HAP1 and HAP2hybrid poplar 717. Both gain-of-function and loss-of-function of PSK2a exhibited growth defects, characterized by reduced plant height and stem diameter, with more severe overall growth defects in OE lines. Consistently, histological analysis demonstrated that cambium activity and secondary xylem development were significantly inhibited in both transgenic lines, as reflected by fewer cambium cell layers, narrower xylem, and fewer vessels in young stems. In addition, genes associated with cambial development, vessel differentiation, and secondary cell wall formation were broadly downregulated, accompanied by altered expression of several hormone-related marker genes in transgenic lines. Together, these findings demonstrate that PSK2a is required for normal cambial activity and xylem development during secondary growth in poplar, providing the first direct genetic evidence for PSK function in woody plant vascular development.
items.authors: Yue S, Tian D, Ma X, Qi C, Wan M, Qi J, Cheng Q, Tian L, Shi X, Zheng B.

items.title: Genome-Wide Identification and Characterization of the Rboh Gene Family in Populus trichocarpa Reveals PtrRbohB Positively Regulates Adventitious Root Development.
items.abstract: Adventitious roots (ARs) are essential for clonal vegetative propagation of woody tree species. Extensive studies have focused on phytohormone and transcription factor regulatory networks during AR development in poplar, yet the regulatory roles of reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling during AR development remain poorly understood. In this study, we performed a genome-wide identification and systematic characterization of the Respiratory Burst Oxidase Homolog (Rboh) gene family in Populus trichocarpa. A total of 10 PtrRbohs were identified and phylogenetically classified into five subfamilies. Expression profiling revealed distinct tissue-specific and stress-responsive expression patterns among PtrRbohs. Functional validation via CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout showed that disruption of PtrRbohB significantly reduced AR length, diameter, and lateral root density in poplar. Heterologous overexpression of PtrRbohB in Arabidopsis thaliana enhanced ROS accumulation, confirming its conserved function in ROS generation. Furthermore, knockout of PtrRohB down-regulated the expression of several AR-positive regulators and up-regulated that of AR-negative regulators in poplar. Collectively, this study provides the direct genetic evidence that Rboh regulates AR formation in poplar, and identifies PtrRbohB as a key positive regulator of AR development. These findings enrich our understanding of woody plant AR formation and provide candidate genes for molecular breeding of poplar rooting traits.
items.authors: Shi R, Ding Y, Guo P, Shang F, Cao S.

items.title: Phenylboronic acid-induced defects in maize roots are independent of rhamnogalacturonan-II dimerization.
items.abstract: Soil boron deficiency is a global abiotic stress, negatively impacting on crop yield. In the dicot model species Arabidopsis thaliana, inhibition of root elongation is one of the earliest symptoms of boron deficiency. In the monocot model maize (Zea mays L.), boron deficiency-induced root defects are widely unexplored. In this study, we assessed boron deficiency-induced defects in the primary root system of maize and tested the suitability of phenylboronic acid (PBA) as boron deficiency mimic by performing phenotypic, histological, molecular, and biochemical analyses. Our analyses showed that boron deficiency and PBA resulted in similar defects in primary root elongation and lateral root density. The PBA-induced defects, however, were much stronger than those induced by boron deficiency, particularly regarding lateral root development. We provide evidence that the PBA-induced defects were caused by the boric acid moiety and show that both boron deficiency and PBA altered the levels of auxin and reactive oxygen species. Strikingly, PBA did not affect rhamnogalacturonan-II (RG-II) dimerization. Interference of boron-mediated RG-II crosslinking, however, was previously proposed to be the mode of action of PBA in planta. Our study shows that PBA is particularly suited for the molecular dissection of lateral root development in maize and suggests that PBA does not mimic known molecular boron deficiency responses.
items.authors: Chu L, Sharma D, Brox A, Brück J, Plotecki F, Schäfer CC, Best NB, Duong HN, Chan YO, Baldauf J, Klammer B, Schaaf G, Angelovici R, Hochholdinger F, Urbanowicz B, Matthes MS.

items.title: EPF/EPFL Peptide Signaling as a Regulatory Node Linking Stomatal Development to Drought and Heat Tolerance in Tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum L.)
items.abstract: Stomatal development and function are tightly regulated by signaling peptides with distinct, overlapping, or antagonistic roles in gas exchange and water balance. EPIDERMAL PATTERNING FACTOR (EPF) / EPF-LIKE ( EPF/EPFL ) family is a founding member of the secreted peptide family that regulates stomatal patterning. The roles of EPF/EPFL genes in tomato responses to drought, heat, and combined drought-heat stress remain largely unexplored. To characterize the EPF/EPFL gene family and elucidate its potential regulatory roles in stomatal development, 15 family members were identified in S. lycopersicum L. All 15 candidate SlEPF proteins contained an EPF-type domain. Of these, 13 exhibited specific matches to the EPF domain, whereas SlEPF6 was classified within the EPF superfamily and SlEPF11 within the STOMAGEN-like superfamily. Phylogenetic analysis grouped EPF genes from diverse plant species into two major clades (A and B), each comprising distinct evolutionary subgroups. GO annotation indicated that most SlEPF genes were involved in stomatal complex development and guard cell differentiation, with molecular functions associated with MAP kinase activity, receptor serine/threonine kinase binding, and receptor ligand activity. Promoter analysis of SlEPF genes identified diverse cis-regulatory elements potentially involved in the regulation of environmental stress responses and plant development. Expression analysis of five putative stress-responsive genes ( SlEPF5, SlEPF8, SlEPF9, SlEPF10 , and SlEPF13 ) revealed distinct transcriptional patterns in the heat-tolerant drought-sensitive Money Maker (MM) and drought-tolerant Ailsa Craig (AC) tomato genotypes under drought, heat, and combined drought-heat stress. In MM, SlEPF5 and SlEPF13 were consistently downregulated across all stress conditions, whereas SlEPF8 was strongly induced under drought and combined stress. In contrast, AC showed broader transcriptional activation, particularly under heat and combined stress. Overall, these contrasting expression profiles suggest genotype- and stress-dependent regulation of SlEPF genes, highlighting their potential involvement in tomato abiotic stress responses.
items.authors: Mostafa, K., Aydin, A., Elbar, O. A., Ain, N. u., KAVAS, M., Robert, H. S.

items.title: Fungal volatiles affect lateral root formation and increase plant tolerance to osmotic stress
items.abstract: Symbiotic fungi communicate with plants via volatile organic compounds (VOCs), even before physical contact. While fungal VOCs are known to promote plant development under control conditions, their effects under abiotic stress remain poorly characterized. Here, we exposed Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings to VOCs from the ectomycorrhizal fungi Laccaria bicolor and Hebeloma cylindrosporum, and the endophyte Serendipita indica, under osmotic stress. Time-course transcriptional analysis revealed a rapid, transient induction of auxin transport genes within 3 days of VOC exposure, with minimal early cytokinin modulation. Using auxin- (aux1-7, axr1-3) and cytokinin-resistant (cre1, arr1-4) mutants, we show that this early response bypasses classic auxin/cytokinin antagonism, promoting lateral root proliferation by day 10 under both control and stress conditions. Transcriptomic profiling indicated that fungal VOCs modulate glucosinolate and leucine metabolism and regulate potassium (HAK5) and iron (IRT1) transporters. Genetic and phenotypic analyses of hak5-2 and akt1-2 mutants, together with nitric oxide signaling components, revealed that potassium transport and nitric oxide-dependent IRT1 regulation are essential for translating VOC perception into developmental responses. These findings underscore the multifaceted mechanisms by which fungal VOCs coordinate plant development and abiotic stress tolerance.
items.authors: Minambres, E., Fermoso-Dominguez, J., Rodriguez-Sufuentes, S., Marco-Montori, P., Lorenzo, O., Calvo-Polanco, M.

items.title: Water stable isotopes reveal the ecohydrological importance of stemflow infiltration for mature and juvenile European beech.
items.abstract: Stemflow of forest trees can contribute a significant fraction of water to forest's water fluxes; however, it is still unclear whether and to what extent trees and their neighbours use stemflow for water uptake and supply. We applied deuterium-enriched stemflow equivalent to a 23-mm throughfall event to adult Fagus sylvatica trees to trace stemflow through the soil and trees. We continuously measured in situ water stable isotopes in soil and xylem water and destructively sampled xylem water in the crowns of adult labelled, nonlabelled F. sylvatica and nonlabelled Picea abies, complemented by destructive xylem water sampling of neighbouring juvenile F. sylvatica. Stemflow water supported up to 5.7 ± 2.1% of daily sap flux of adult F. sylvatica trees labelled at the stem base and was detectable in xylem water for several weeks. In the soil, deuterium-enriched stemflow was present at a maximum distance of 0.40 m from the labelled tree. Moreover, nonlabelled juvenile trees within a distance of 2 m showed uptake of labelled water, indicating rooting into soil compartments affected by stemflow. We demonstrate the importance of stemflow as a water source for both adult and neighbouring juvenile F. sylvatica, even when soil water is not limiting.
items.authors: Haberstroh S, Keller S, Kinzinger L, Mach J, Kühnhammer K, Weiler M, Orlowski N, Werner C.

items.title: Lignin Derivatives in Beech, Eucalyptus and Oak Wood Hydrochar: Mild Solvolysis and Characterization.
items.abstract: This study investigates lignin-derived fractions obtained from the hydrochars of beech (Fagus sylvatica L.), eucalyptus (Eucalyptus camaldulensis) and oak (Quercus cerris L.) following hydrothermal carbonization and mild acidolysis. The aim was to understand the structural, molecular, and thermal properties of the recovered material and to compare how botanical origin influences it. FTIR analysis revealed consistent aromatic signatures across all samples; HP-SEC revealed species-dependent differences in molecular weight distributions, although the overall molecular weight range remained comparable among species; 2D NMR further verified the lignin origin of the isolated fractions, while TGA indicated comparable thermal behaviour among the three biomasses. The whole study shows how hydrothermal carbonization followed by mild solvolysis produces lignin-derivative fractions, highlighting both the potential of this approach for lignin recovery and the need for more efficient methods to obtain higher-integrity lignin suitable for advanced material applications.
items.authors: Pierpaoli V, Grilc M, Tofani G, Likozar B, Jasiukaitytė-Grojzdek E, Romagnoli M.

items.title: Canopy-scale VPD reduction in a mature forest alters stomatal response to soil drought in Pinus sylvestris L.
items.abstract: Understanding how trees respond to interacting soil and atmospheric droughts is crucial for predicting forest resilience under climate change. However, no experiment has yet jointly manipulated vapor pressure deficit (VPD) and soil moisture in forests, limiting our ability to disentangle their effects. We investigated how c. 130-yr-old trees respond to coupled soil and atmospheric drought with a rainfall and VPD manipulation in an unmanaged forest. Using fine mist sprayers installed at canopy height, we reduced VPD by 24% in combination with throughfall exclusion (-50% precipitation) or irrigation (+100% precipitation) in mature Pinus sylvestris trees. We monitored tree water status, canopy conductance, and stomatal responses throughout the growing season. With irrigation, VPD reduction did not affect tree water relations. Under soil drought, trees exposed to reduced VPD used more water and reached lower predawn water potentials (ΨPD). This was accompanied by two parallel mechanisms: more frequently open stomata (at low-VPD intensities); and a modification in the stomatal response to VPD. Moreover, reduced VPD resulted in shifted stomatal closure from a predawn water potential of -1.2 to -1.5 MPa. Exposure to low atmospheric demand affected trees' response to soil drought, providing observational evidences from joint air-soil drought manipulation in natura.
items.authors: Bortolami G, Schaub M, Gisler J, Milano A, Bachofen C, Deluigi J, Favre P, Meusburger K, Gessler A, Hunziker S, Kükenbrink D, Kullberg AT, Marty M, Peters RL, Poretti A, Schuler P, Trotsiuk V, Vallicrosa H, Zweifel R, Grossiord C.

items.title: Tree species composition and nutrient uptake influence soil nutrient availability, even under contrasted levels of water availability
items.abstract: Temporal asynchrony within a vegetation period, such as when mixing trees with contrasting leaf phenology (i.e. deciduous and evergreen species), may play an important role in accelerating belowground nutrient cycling in mixed-species forests. However, forests are increasingly impacted by drought, and how mixing effects may be modified by changes in water availability is unknown. Using an 11-year-old experimental plantation in southwestern France, we tested the interactive effect of stand composition (monocultures of each Pinus pinaster and Betula pendula, and the mixture of the two species) and water availability (via irrigation) on various belowground processes. We quantified soil nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) availability with ion-exchange resins in the growing vs dormant periods, net mineralization with an in situ soil incubation method every 4-6 weeks from April to September, and N uptake by trees using two in situ 15 N soil labeling campaigns, one at budburst and one at peak leaf expansion in summer. The methods were implemented at several time points, in order to elucidate potential temporal complementarity in the mixture. We found differences in soil nutrient availability between different species compositions, with pure pine generally having higher mineral N, and pure birch having higher available P under high water availability. These differences were unlikely due to increases in net nutrient mineralization, as these rates were similar among treatments. Instead, differences in tree growth and canopy covering between species compositions, and thus different nutrient uptake needs may be the main drivers for the soil nutrient availability trends. The 15 N labeling experiment revealed a competitive advantage for pine in the mixture at budburst, with higher N uptake than pine in monocultures, without negatively impacting birch uptake. This advantage was then lost once birch's leaves were out in the early summer. We conclude that the timing of nutrient needs and uptake of species within a mixture, such as between a broadleaf deciduous and an evergreen conifer, may be a stronger driver than mineralization for soil nutrient availability in a mixture, even under two contrasted levels of water availability.
items.authors: Maxwell, T. L., Fanin, N., Munson, A. D., Lambrot, C., Trichet, P., Bernier, F., Severin, L., Augusto, L.

items.title: Heterologous Expression of Saussurea involucrata SiPIP1;5b Enhances Freezing Tolerance in Arabidopsis and Chilling Tolerance in Tomato.
items.abstract: Low temperature is a major constraint limiting the productivity and distribution of crops, and aquaporins have emerged as important determinants of plant stress tolerance. Saussurea involucrata, an alpine plant adapted to extreme low-temperature environments, provides a valuable source of cold-tolerance genes, yet the contribution of its PIP1-type plasma membrane aquaporins to freezing and chilling tolerance in heterologous systems has not been established. Here, we isolated SiPIP1;5b, a PIP1-type plasma membrane intrinsic protein from S. involucrata, and constitutively overexpressed it in Arabidopsis thaliana and tomato (Solanum lycopersicum). Under freezing treatment (-4 °C, 4 h), SiPIP1;5b-overexpressing Arabidopsis lines showed markedly higher survival rates (72.0-81.5%) than the wild type (36.2%), together with lower relative electrolyte leakage and malondialdehyde (MDA) content and higher chlorophyll content. Under chilling stress (0 °C, 4 h), transgenic tomato plants likewise exhibited reduced electrolyte leakage and MDA accumulation, elevated activities of superoxide dismutase, catalase, and peroxidase, and increased proline content relative to wild-type plants. These results indicate that SiPIP1;5b enhances freezing and chilling tolerance and is associated with improved membrane stability, reduced accumulation of excessive reactive oxygen species, and enhanced antioxidant and osmoprotective responses. Our findings establish SiPIP1;5b as a promising candidate gene for improving low-temperature tolerance in crops.
items.authors: Wu X, Wang S, Yin B, Zhou W, Zhang Z, Xin H, Zhang H, Cui B, Xia W, Liu R, Li J, Zhu J.

items.title: HAR1 receptor kinase links nodule autoregulation with repression of auxin signaling and lateral root development.
items.abstract: Nitrogen-fixing root nodules develop as lateral organs on legume roots and their formation is restricted by autoregulation of nodulation (AON), a systemic mechanism with unclear evolutionary origins. We identify Lotus japonicus NUCLEAR FACTOR Y subunit A4 (NF-YA4) gene as a central target of the leucine-rich repeat receptor kinase HAR1, which controls both AON and root system architecture. Under nonsymbiotic conditions, HAR1 suppresses expression of NF-YA4 and its close paralog NF-YA1, at least in part through a miR169-dependent mechanism, mirroring the Arabidopsis CLAVATA1/2-miR169-NF-YA module. Loss of HAR1 leads to NF-YA4 overexpression, broad transcriptional reprogramming, and induction of LATERAL ORGAN BOUNDARIES DOMAIN, STYLISH, and YUCCA auxin biosynthesis genes, enhancing auxin signaling and lateral root development. Grafting experiments show that HAR1 constrains NF-YA4-mediated branching both locally in roots and systemically from shoots. Because NF-YA4 functions partly redundantly with NF-YA1 to mediate nodule emergence, our results suggest a model in which duplication and neofunctionalization of an ancestral NF-YA-dependent pathway controlling lateral root development facilitated its recruitment to the nodulation program. They also raise the possibility that AON could have evolved, at least in part, through the co-option of a LRR-RK/miR169/NF-YA regulatory module that limited lateral root development.
items.authors: Therrien JA, Huebert T, Janakirama P, Kaplanoglu E, Fechete LI, Kohalmi S, Andersen SU, Stougaard J, Ross L, Szczyglowski K.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
also: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Characterization of the Populus PLCP Gene Family and the Function of PtrXCP2A in Wood Formation.
items.abstract: Papain-like cysteine proteases (PLCPs) are a class of proteolytic enzymes that are involved in plant stress, immunity, growth and development processes. Compared to the extensive research on herbaceous plants, little is known about the PLCPs in trees, and the involvement of PLCPs in wood formation still needs to be confirmed. Here, 40 PLCPs were recognized in the genome of Populus trichocarpa, which can be divided into seven subfamilies with identified members: RD21, CEP, XCP, XBCP3, SAG12, RD19 and ALP. The genes in each subfamily exhibited similar gene structures, conserved motifs and domain compositions. Chromosome mapping analysis revealed that tandem and segmental duplications played crucial roles in expanding the PLCP family in Populus. Expression profiling, RT-qPCR verification and GUS activity analysis revealed that several PtrPLCPs were preferentially or highly expressed in the secondary xylem of the stem. Furthermore, we characterised PtrXCP2A overexpression in poplars and found that overexpression of PtrXCP2A accelerates the loss of xylem fiber viability, reduces fiber cell wall thickness and lignin content, but increases the saccharification yield of wood cell walls in transgenic poplar. These findings offer valuable information for future functional studies on the PLCP gene family, and an alternative gene for engineering lignocellulosic biomass for wood utilisation.
items.authors: Cao S, Wu X, Wang X, Guo P, Shang F.

items.title: CLE25 peptide enhances drought tolerance in cotton (Gossypium hirsutum) by inducing abscisic acid biosynthesis.
items.abstract: Drought is a leading abiotic factor affecting agricultural productivity. While AtCLE25 enhances drought tolerance by inducing abscisic acid (ABA) accumulation in Arabidopsis thaliana, the mechanisms by which GhCLE25 regulates drought tolerance in cotton (Gossypium hirsutum) remain unclear. In this study, the role of GhCLE25 in cotton drought tolerance was investigated using virus-induced gene silencing and exogenous CLE25 peptide treatment. GhCLE25 expression was significantly induced in both roots and leaves under natural and polyethylene glycol 6000 (PEG 6000)-simulated drought. Silencing GhCLE25 inhibited stomatal closure, increased water loss, and decreased drought tolerance, whereas exogenous CLE25 improved drought tolerance by inducing stomatal closure. Consistently, ABA content was decreased in GhCLE25-silenced plants but increased in CLE25-treated plants. Silencing GhCLE25 downregulated ABA biosynthetic genes (NCED2, NCED3, NCED5, and NCED9) but upregulated the ABA catabolic gene CYP707A1. Conversely, the expression of ABA biosynthetic and catabolic genes showed an opposite trend under CLE25 peptide treatment. Moreover, the ABA-responsive genes Late Embryogenesis Abundant (LEA) and RD29B were reduced in GhCLE25-silencing plants but increased following CLE25 treatment. Thus, these results suggest that GhCLE25 may regulate ABA levels by modulating the expression of ABA metabolism-related genes, which could further regulate stomatal closure and ABA-responsive gene expression to enhance drought tolerance in cotton.
items.authors: Duan X, Hu Q, Luo Z, Tang W, Lu H, Ma C, Kong X.

items.title: Towards understanding stomatal decoupling under extreme heat: integrating stomatal kinetics, leaf light responses, and the role of stomatal versus cuticular conductance
items.abstract: · Earth's forests are increasingly exposed to hotter drought events, causing unprecedented dieback of trees and forests. Evidence of stomatal decoupling at high leaf temperatures (T leaf ) is mounting, but the driving mechanisms and variability across species are unknown. · We experimentally imposed heat and drought stress onto two rainforest and two semi-arid tree species in a glasshouse study to better understand accelerated water loss at high T leaf by measuring plant thermal and hydraulic balance. · Stomatal decoupling at high T leaf occurred in two species, including the most anisohydric species, but did not occur in a vulnerable rainforest species. Accelerated leaf water loss occurred predominantly through open stomata, rather than the cuticle, but some species prioritised thermal acclimation over leaf thermoregulation during heat stress. This suggests decoupling occurs only in species with high capacity for transpirational cooling (>5°C), or alternatively, that full sunlight is required for stomatal decoupling. · The maximum rate of light-induced stomatal opening was up to two times faster, while dark-induced stomatal closing was 14 minutes slower on average in leaves at 34°C, relative to 25°C. Stomatal kinetics are an overlooked trait that may help to better predict accelerated water loss under high T leaf across species.
items.authors: Marchin, R. M., Ossola, A., Tjoelker, M. G., Ellsworth, D. S.

items.title: MIR2111a-mediated low-phosphate adaptation is linked to enhanced leaf phosphorus-use efficiency and growth maintenance in poplar.
items.abstract: Inorganic phosphate (Pi) limitation constrains tree growth and necessitates coordinated physiological and developmental adjustments to maintain Pi homeostasis. However, the role of miRNA-mediated regulation in low-phosphate responses remains poorly understood in woody species. In this study, we investigated the role of MIR2111a in hybrid poplar (Populus tremula × P. alba; hereafter poplar 717). Overexpression (OE) and CRISPR/Cas9-generated mutant (CR) lines were generated to assess its function in low-phosphate adaptation. Among the MIR2111 family members, MIR2111a was more strongly induced under low-phosphate conditions, particularly in young leaves. Under phosphate limitation, the OE lines maintained higher biomass and showed increased root biomass allocation, whereas the CR lines exhibited enhanced root elongation but reduced overall biomass. Notably, the OE lines maintained lower leaf Pi content but significantly higher leaf phosphorus-use efficiency and ATP levels, indicating more efficient Pi utilization rather than increased Pi accumulation. In addition, under low-phosphate conditions, the OE lines exhibited reduced malondialdehyde (MDA) content and elevated superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity compared with poplar 717, suggesting decreased lipid peroxidation and enhanced antioxidant enzyme activity. Leaf transcriptome analysis further revealed that Pi-responsive genes involved in Pi signaling, transport, and energy metabolism were differentially regulated between OE and CR lines. Collectively, these results support an important role for MIR2111a in low-phosphate adaptation and biomass maintenance in poplar, providing new insights into miRNA-mediated phosphate responses in woody plants.
items.authors: Wang J, Chen R, Jiang Z, Yu S, Huang Z, Cheng J, Wang Y, Zheng B, Shi X.

items.title: Allelic tuning of PtoRLK609 kinase activity shapes adaptive xylem remodeling in Populus tomentosa.
items.abstract: Climate change poses unprecedented challenges to perennial trees. However, the molecular mechanisms by which trees achieve long-term adaptive xylem remodeling remain poorly understood. Here, using transcriptomics and population genomics in 302 Populus tomentosa accessions sampled from three climatically distinct subpopulations, we identified receptor-like kinases (RLKs) associated with climate-related variation in xylem lignification. Among 49 candidates, the wall-associated kinase PtoRLK609 showed among the strongest signatures of population differentiation, a pattern consistent with climate-associated selection. Two major PtoRLK609 haplotypes, defined by four linked missense variants, showed marked geographic differentiation, with PtoRLK609Hap2 reaching fixation or near-fixation in northern populations that experience drier and cooler climates, and was associated with elevated lignin content. PtoRLK609 phosphorylates the transcription factor PtoERF105 at Ser171, which promotes its nuclear accumulation and enhances activation of the lignin biosynthesis genes PtoLAC4 and PtoCCoAOMT1, as well as the vessel development regulator PtoVND7. The PtoRLK609Hap2 protein variant showed higher kinase activity and more efficient phosphorylation of PtoERF105 than PtoRLK609Hap1, linking natural protein variation to differential transcriptional output. Consistent with this mechanism, gain- and loss-of-function analyses showed that PtoRLK609 promotes secondary cell wall lignification, elevates the syringyl-to-guaiacyl (S/G) ratio, increases vessel density, and is associated with better maintenance of stem water status under controlled water deficit. These findings characterize a PtoRLK609-PtoERF105 phosphorylation module associated with xylem remodeling and identify an RLK locus that is a strong candidate for contributing to climate-associated divergence in perennial trees.
items.authors: Qi W, Wen Z, Huang W, Ren T, Xiao L, Fang Y, Li Y, Yuan X, Cheng W, He W, Quan M, Du Q, Ingvarsson PK, El-Kassaby YA, Zhang D.

items.title: Nuclear importin α1 AtIMPA1 regulates stomatal reopening to defend against Pst DC3000 by orchestrating ABA signaling.
items.abstract: Importin α family proteins serve as essential carriers for transporting specific disease-resistant proteins into the nucleus, enabling these proteins to function properly. However, whether importin α proteins are involved in plant immunity remains unclear. Here, we characterized a guard cell-expressed protein importin α1 AtIMPA1, which contributed to resistance against Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000 (Pst DC3000). When dip-inoculated with Pst DC3000, the impa1 mutants exhibited increased susceptibility, along with significant stomatal reopening induced by the phytotoxin coronatine (COR) secreted by Pst DC3000; while overexpression of AtIMPA1 enhanced resistance to Pst DC3000 with compromised stomatal reopening induced by COR. Notably, following syringe-infiltration of Pst DC3000, the impa1 mutants showed increased resistance, whereas overexpression lines were more susceptible to Pst DC3000, indicating that COR-triggered stomatal reopening is a primary determinant in AtIMPA1-mediated disease resistance. Further investigations revealed that AtIMPA1 regulated COR-triggered stomatal reopening is linked to abscisic acid (ABA) signaling. Mutation of AtIMPA1 attenuated the ABA-mediated inhibition of root length and seed germination, and disrupted the ABA-induced protein abundance and localization of the ABA-responsive protein, supporting its role in regulating the ABA response. These findings shed light on the functional significance of AtIMPA1 in COR-triggered stomatal reopening and provided new insights into how importin α proteins orchestrate ABA signaling to regulate plant immunity.
items.authors: Zhang T, Wang K, Guan Y, Zhang J, Tetteh C, Liu C, Zhang C, Jin P, Luo S, Wang Y, Zhang H.
items.journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology

items.title: Enhancing the Resistance of Soybean Plants to Waterlogging Stress Using Gamma-Irradiated Priestia megaterium.
items.abstract: The rhizosphere of Fabaceae contains plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) that regulate phytohormone balance, nutrient acquisition, and biofilm formation, thereby contributing to plant development and stress tolerance. Although Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) and exopolysaccharides (EPS) are well-established PGPR-associated factors, their combined contributions to waterlogging tolerance in soybean remain unclear. In this study, Bacillus-like PGPR were isolated from the rhizosphere of soybean plants cultivated in field soil, and Priestia megaterium and P. aryabhattai were identified among Bacillus-like bacteria based on strong EPS production, a PGPR-associated trait. The P. megaterium isolate S135-A1-2 was subjected to gamma-ray irradiation to generate mutants, from which mutants #6 (increased EPS), #8 (increased IAA), and #12 (increased EPS and IAA) were selected for further analysis. Mutant #8 produced 4.48 μg/mL IAA, a 3.6-fold increase over the parental strain, and protease and siderophore activities were also evaluated as additional PGPR-associated traits. Their plant growth-promoting traits were evaluated using pot assays under waterlogging conditions. Inoculation with mutants #6 and #8 increased lateral root development and root biomass relative to the parental strain, whereas mutant #12 showed a distinct response pattern associated with dual-trait enhancement under waterlogging stress. After 7 days of waterlogging, mutant #12 showed higher chlorophyll-related values than mutants #6 and #8. These results indicate that gamma-irradiated P. megaterium mutants can differentially modify soybean root system responses to flooding stress, supporting gamma-ray irradiation as a useful approach for developing PGPR with improved functions for agricultural applications under waterlogging stresses.
items.authors: Wang ST, Chen LG, Shu HY, Lu SY, Chen YC, Su MC, Wang SH.

items.title: SAMDC Activity Is Involved in the Melatonin-Mediated Tolerance of Barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) Seedlings to Osmotic Stress.
items.abstract: Exogenous melatonin can elevate the tolerance of plants to drought stress. The mechanism of melatonin-mediated tolerance has been extensively studied. Numerous studies have shown that melatonin treatment can increase contents of osmotic adjustment substances, alleviate oxidative damage, and maintain photosynthetic characteristics of plants under drought stress. However, a research gap remains, i.e., whether melatonin plays the above-mentioned functions by regulating polyamine metabolism. In the present study, S-adenosylmethionine decarboxylase (SAMDC) activity and the levels of spermine and spermidine were detected in melatonin-treated barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) seedlings under polyethylene glycol-6000, which was used to simulate drought stress. The aim was to probe whether polyamine metabolism was involved in the process of melatonin-mediated osmotic stress tolerance. The results indicated that exogenous melatonin improved the tolerance of barley seedlings to osmotic stress, coupled with increasing content of proline, alleviating oxidative damage and maintaining the photosynthetic characteristics of barley seedlings. More importantly, melatonin elevated the activity of SAMDC, and thereby the contents of spermine and spermidine. Thus, it was speculated that melatonin functioned by regulating polyamine metabolism. The hypothesis was further reinforced by the results of inhibitor experiments. Inhibitor methylglyoxal-bis (guanylhydrazone), which can inhibit SAMDC activity strongly and specifically, not only inhibited the melatonin-induced increases in the activity of SAMDC and the levels of spermine and spermidine, but also inhibited melatonin-induced increases in antioxidant ability, proline content, and photosynthetic capacity. The relationship between SAMDC activity and the effects of melatonin on proline content, antioxidant ability, and leaf photosynthetic characteristics was further explored and is discussed below. Therefore, it could be concluded that SAMDC might be involved in the melatonin-mediated tolerance of barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) seedlings to osmotic stress.
items.authors: Chang Y, Yu J, Hua C, Liu H.

items.title: Differential hydraulic and carbon economic strategies among four oak species.
items.abstract: BackgroundThe fluctuations of precipitation will become more erratic and dramatic, threatening the growth and survival of forest species. Plants usually integrate water and carbon management strategies to deal with environmental variations. The hydraulic strategies of woody plants would modify their carbon capture and allocation patterns, thus characterizing divergent strategies in water and carbon use economy could elucidate the differential responses to climate change among closely related species. To decipher possible correlations between functional traits relating to plant hydraulics and carbon economics, we selected four oak species (one native species, Quercus dentata, and three exotic species, Q. rubra, Q. robur, and Q. palustris) growing in an Oak Nursery to explore trait associations in hydraulic and carbon economics, and to contrast strategy variations among four species.ResultsOur results showed a trade-off between leaf gas exchange rate and water use efficiency, where fast gas exchange related to fluctuating water potential. In carbon allocation patterns, higher Huber values could supply sufficient water in leaves, thereby maintaining water potential stable.ConclusionsCompared to the exotic oaks, Q. dentata adopted a relatively conservative strategy, embodying high water use efficiency, stable water potential, and leaves with smaller but denser stomata. However, Q. rubra was conservative and rapid-responsive, Q. robur was potentially drought-tolerant, and Q. palustris employed a strategy of less drought-resistant but might be more competitive in the face of abundant resources. Integrating these findings into global conservation efforts will lead to the development of adaptive management practices that foster tree species with better adaptation to environmental variations.
items.authors: Li Q, Sun X, Jiang J, Feng Z, Sun W, Huang Y, Du N.

items.title: Combined effects of drought and insect herbivory on oak leaf endophytic communities and performance.
items.abstract: Leaf-associated microbiota are considered sensitive indicators of how plants respond to their environment. Yet, plants can be exposed to a wide range of biotic and abiotic stresses whose independent and combined effects on plant microbiota remain poorly understood, as do their cumulative consequences for plant performance. We conducted an experiment to expose saplings of four oak species to drought and herbivory by a piercing-sucking insect. We assessed the effect of water deficit on herbivory, as well as the individual and combined effects of water deficit and herbivory on fungal endophytic communities. To evaluate the cumulative impacts of biotic and abiotic stresses on plant performance, and the potential of the fungal endophytic communities as an indicator of plant responses to stress, we measured photosynthetic capacity, growth, and the accumulation of non-structural carbohydrates in twigs at the end of the growing season. Water deficit had no effect on insect herbivory but induced a decrease in the diversity of the leaf-associated fungal community. In contrast, herbivory shifted the composition of fungal communities through species replacement or addition depending on oak species. Herbivory altered photosynthesis, whereas drought but not herbivory reduced oak growth. None of these stresses influenced the storage of non-structural carbohydrates. Leaf-associated fungi responded to both stresses. However, the underlying mechanisms appeared to differ and the association with oak performance was weak. Overall, our study suggests a certain degree of resilience in trees subjected to interacting stresses, while also highlighting vulnerabilities that may have implications for tree health over the long term.
items.authors: Barlier T, Castagneyrol B, Carton J, Burlett R, Bonnard O, Schimann H.

items.title: Transient overexpression and silencing of tomato SlGLP11-1 gene reveal its crucial role in mediating ROS homeostasis driven disease resistance
items.abstract: Abstract Germin and germin- like proteins (GLPs) are known to play various roles in plant development and in response to biotic and abiotic stress. Many GLPs have been reported to show differential expression in response to pathogen infections, indicating their direct roles in host- pathogen interactions. Despite their significant roles in plant immunity, the tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum L.) GLP members have not been studied comprehensively at the genome- wide scale. Also, very few reports exist on the functions and activities of tomato GLP gene family members. In this study, GLP family members in tomato were analysed and a standardised nomenclature for tomato GLP genes was defined. The chromosomal distribution of GLP genes in tomato was determined, and a phylogenetic analysis was performed. In addition, the in silico subcellular localization of GLPs in tomato was predicted, and gene expression was examined in response to different phytohormone treatments and pathogen infection. Finally, we identified candidate pathogen- responsive SlGLPs and functionally characterized SlGLP11-1 . Transient overexpression of SlGLP11-1 in Nicotiana leaves enhanced resistance against Botrytis cinerea . Similarly transient silencing of SlGLP11-1 by virus induced gene silencing (VIGS) in tomato leaves increased susceptibility to Botrytis cinerea infection. We also, estimated endogenous H 2 O 2 levels and catalase activity in the transient SlGLP11- 1 overexpressed and silenced leaves of Nicotiana benthamiana and tomato respectively, all with and without Botrytis infection. Our results establish that SlGLP11 -1 functions as a positive regulator of ROS-mediated plant defence by promoting H 2 O 2 accumulation during both basal and pathogen challenged conditions, with catalase activity tracking H 2 O 2 levels as a secondary antioxidant response. This study will serve as a foundation for future functional investigations of tomato GLP family members playing role in the plant immunity.
items.authors: Prajapati P, Khobragade T, Kamble A.

items.title: Transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling reveals early responses of tomato plants elicited by compost-derived bacteria
items.abstract: Compost produced from biowaste has a defined microbiota, and some bacterial species may represent promising resources for low-input crop systems. However, their effects on plant physiology are poorly investigated and remain difficult to predict from standard bacterial traits alone. We isolated several bacterial strains ( Bacillus sonorensis, Glutamicibacter arilaitensis, and Kocuria rhizophila ) from biowaste compost and examined their early effects on tomato seedlings under controlled in vitro conditions. Responses were assessed by root phenotyping, root and shoot transcriptomics, and mass spectrometry-based profiling of primary metabolites in plant tissues, root exudates and bacterial culture filtrates. B. sonorensis induces the broadest response, reducing primary root length and lateral root number and density and triggering broad transcriptional changes related to metabolism, redox balance, hormone signalling and defence-associated pathways. G. arilaitensis elicits a more selective, tissue-dependent response, whereas K. rhizophila has limited phenotypic and transcriptional effects at this stage. All isolates reshape primary metabolism, with recurrent effects on amino acid-, carbohydrate- and lipid-related pathways, together with isolate-specific changes in root exudate composition. This study characterises the early molecular and metabolic responses of tomato to compost-derived bacteria and identifies common and strain-specific physiological signatures that provide a foundation for future studies under biotic and abiotic stress.
items.authors: Ghirardello, G., Araniti, F., Cipriani, R., Zanardi, W., Bonato, T., Baldan, B., Nigris, S.

items.title: Decoding microbial diversity in roots of rice plants under flooded conditions: influence of the host genotype, root compartment, and mycorrhizal association.
items.abstract: Rice is a vital staple for more than half of the world's population, uniquely adapted to grow under flooded conditions. Our current understanding of root-associated microbiomes in rice plants under flooded conditions (anaerobic rice) is, however, limited. While rice plants are capable of establishing symbiotic associations with arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi, also under flooded conditions, little is known about the impact that mycorrhizal associations might have on the root microbiome. Here, we used metagenomic sequencing to characterize the root-associated microbiomes of cultivated rice grown under flooded conditions. The root endosphere and rhizosphere compartments were found to harbor distinct microbial communities, with bacterial taxa comprising approximately 95% of the total microbial community. At the phylum level, the root bacteriome was primarily composed of Pseudomonadota (Alphaproteobacteria, Betaproteobacteria, and Gammaproteobacteria), followed by Actinomycetota. The fungal microbiome was dominated by Ascomycota (Sordariomycetes, Eurotiomycetes, and Dothideomycetes) and Basidiomycota. Both root compartment and host genotype significantly influenced microbiome composition, with most genotype-specific recruitment occurring at the species level. These associations were further reshaped in plants pre-inoculated with the AM fungus Rhizophagus irregularis. Co-occurrence networks revealed a genotype-dependent effect in the complexity of microbial taxa in mycorrhizal rice plants. Key microbial species primarily involved in methane production and nutrient cycling (e.g., phosphate-solubilizing bacteria and nitrogen-cycling bacteria) residing in roots of flooded rice were identified. Functional analysis of gene abundance related to those microbial communities revealed compartmentalization, with nutrient-cycling bacteria being more prevalent at the endosphere. Overall, this study demonstrated that the rice genotype, root compartment, and mycorrhizal condition shape the root microbiome in rice plants, ultimately influencing holobiont dynamics in flooded rice fields.ImportancePlant roots harbor a large diversity of microorganisms that strongly influence plant health and improve stress tolerance. Among them, root colonization by arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi enhances mineral nutrition and mitigates environmental stress. Although most rice cultivated worldwide is grown under anaerobic conditions (flooded fields), investigation of microbial communities inhabiting root-associated compartments of flooded rice, including AM fungi, has received only little attention. Here, we demonstrated that the rice genotype, root compartment, and mycorrhizal condition markedly influence the microbiome in roots of rice plants in flooded conditions, thus illustrating the potential of the rice plant to shape its root-associated microbiome. Differential root-associated microbiomes of commercial rice varieties include microbes primarily associated with methane production and nutrient cycling. Elucidation of factors influencing root-associated microbiomes in flooded rice systems, including their association with AM fungi, offers practical guidance for exploiting root-associated microbial communities for sustainable rice cultivation while reducing reliance on agrochemicals.
items.authors: Busturia I, Martín-Cardoso H, Domingo C, Garcia-Molina A, San Segundo B.

items.title: A molecular rheostat of ABA signaling coordinates the trade-off between stem growth and drought adaptation.
items.abstract: BackgroundPlants balance vegetative growth and stress responses through antagonistic phytohormone crosstalk, notably between abscisic acid (ABA) and cytokinin. However, the genetic architecture and molecular mechanisms driving this adaptive trade-off, particularly in perennial trees, remain elusive.ResultsIntegrating genome-environment and genome-wide association studies across 302 Populus tomentosa accessions, we identify PtoAG1 as a pleiotropic regulator of climate adaptation and stem growth. A naturally occurring frameshift mutation abolishes its repressor function, driving geographical niche differentiation by enhancing growth in humid habitats. Mechanistically, PtoAG1 acts as a molecular rheostat. Under drought, ABA-activated PtoSnRK2.2 phosphorylates PtoMYB84 to transactivate PtoAG1. PtoAG1 then represses the cytokinin-signaling regulator PtoRR12, consequently releasing its inhibition of PtoSnRK2.2. This positive feedback further suppresses vegetative growth under stress while amplifying ABA responses via PtoAREB3. Concurrently, PtoAG1 directly represses PtoAREB3 as a transcriptional brake to maintain signaling homeostasis. Evolutionary analyses reveal that PtoMYB84 and PtoAG1 constitute a tightly linked cis-regulatory module conserved across eudicots. Functional analysis on AG1 orthologs in poplar, Arabidopsis, rice, and tomato demonstrates conserved cross-species utility: loss-of-function increases vegetative biomass but overexpression significantly boosts drought resilience.ConclusionsOur study identifies a hierarchical crosstalk mechanism bridging ABA and cytokinin signaling to optimize environmental fitness. The evolutionarily conserved MYB84-AG1 cis-regulatory module establishes a versatile, translatable genetic target for precision breeding of climate-resilient and high-yielding crops.
items.authors: Lv C, He Y, Zhang D, Zhang M, Yuan M, Zhong L, Tian C, Zhou J, Huang R, Jin Z, Li P, Lu W, Xiao L, Li J, Quan M, Li Z, Zhao R, Du L, Liu LJ, Zhang D, Du Q.

items.title: Co-formulated plant growth regulators applied before the juvenile-to-adult transition prime microRNA-mediated stress defence and improve yield in sorghum (Sorghum bicolor L. Moench)
items.abstract: Abstract Sorghum (Sorghum bicolor L. Moench) yield improvement has stagnated despite the crop's inherent advantages as a C4 species adapted to water-limited environments. In Australia, yield gaps between water-limited potential and attainable on-farm yields average 59% of potential, representing a major unrealised opportunity (Garba et al., 2025). Biotic and abiotic stress remain primary yield limiters, and existing genetic and management tools have failed to close this gap. This study reports findings from eleven replicated field trials conducted at multiple experimental sites across three production regions of South-East Queensland, Australia, over seven seasons (2014-15 to 2020-21), evaluating the response of commercial grain sorghum to co-formulated plant growth regulators (PGRs) -- comprising a gibberellin biosynthesis inhibitor and an ethylene precursor -- applied at the 2-4 leaf growth stage so that the absorbed phytohormones could become physiologically active as plants entered the fourth- to fifth-leaf juvenile-to-adult (JA) phase transition. The central hypothesis was that exogenous PGRs applied during this early developmental window interact with endogenous microRNA-mediated signalling pathways -- particularly miR156 and miR172 -- to prime the plant's own defence and resource allocation systems for the remainder of the growing season. Across six commercial varieties and highly variable seasonal conditions including drought years, ANOVA confirmed statistically significant treatment effects on yield or associated agronomic outcomes across the trial programme. Yield responses ranged from 107% to 134% of the untreated control in responsive trials, with T3 (medium-low rate) the most consistently effective treatment across seasons, experimental sites, and varieties. Under severe drought, treated plants showed significantly reduced grain screenings (from 27% to 14%) and enhanced staygreen, consistent with a shift from growth optimisation to stress defence. Broad-spectrum disease suppression was recorded across multiple pathogens -- consistent with activation of systemic acquired resistance pathways mediated by ethylene and jasmonic acid signalling. The variety independence of responses, the adaptive switching between growth and defence modes across seasons, and the timing specificity of the early application window collectively support the proposed priming mechanism. These findings contribute a management dimension to the G×E×M framework needed to break the established sorghum yield barrier, offering yield improvements equivalent to approximately 20 years of conventional genetic progress through a single, scalable, variety-independent intervention.
items.authors: McMurrich D.

items.title: Elevational variations in fine root production, turnover, and rhizosphere autotrophic soil respiration in subalpine forests.
items.abstract: Although aboveground forest biomass and growth decrease with elevation, elevational variation in belowground production has not been well studied. Information on belowground production is necessary to clarify the production and carbon cycling processes of forests in mountainous regions. This study aimed to clarify the elevational variations in fine root biomass, fine root production rate, and rhizosphere autotrophic soil respiration at four elevations (1600, 2000, 2300, and 2500 m above sea level) in central Japan. The fine root production rate was measured using the ingrowth core method. The lower three elevations were characterized by subalpine coniferous forests, whereas light-demanding dwarf pine Pinus pumila and deciduous hardwood Betula ermanii were characteristic of the highest elevation (i.e., treeline ecotone). The aboveground biomass, fine root biomass and fine root production rates were lower at higher elevations. The fine root biomass and fine root production rate per fine root biomass per day during the growing season were also lower at higher elevations, indicating that the lower fine root production rates at high elevations were associated with shorter growing seasons and lower turnover (i.e., fine root production rates per biomass). The rhizosphere autotrophic soil respiration rate per fine root biomass was positively correlated with soil temperature and was higher at higher elevations at all soil temperatures, indicating higher root activities during the growing season at higher elevations. The results of this study will contribute to the understanding of elevational changes in root dynamics in the temperate zone.
items.authors: Masuta H, Makita N, Takahashi K.

items.title: Genome-Wide Identification and Expression Analysis of Aquaporin Gene Family in 84K Poplar.
items.abstract: Aquaporins (AQPs) mediate the transmembrane transport of water and diverse small molecules, playing essential roles in plant growth and development and stress responses. However, their genome-wide organization and evolution at the subgenome level in hybrid 84K poplar (Populus alba × Populus tremula var. glandulosa) remain incompletely characterized. Based on the telomere-to-telomere genome of 84K poplar, we identified 94 PagAQPs, with 46 and 48 members in the A and G subgenomes, respectively. Phylogenetic analysis classified them into five subfamilies unevenly distributed across 29 chromosomes, with PagPIP and PagTIP being the two largest subfamilies. Most PagAQPs were retained as corresponding A/G allelic pairs, whereas few exhibit subgenome-specific retention. Valid Ka/Ks ratios for 38 allelic pairs and 59 paralogous gene pairs were all below 1, indicating predominant purifying selection. Gene structure, conserved motifs, and substrate-recognition residues showed conservation within subfamilies and divergence among subfamilies. The promoters contained predicted cis-acting elements associated with light, phytohormone and abiotic stress responses. Expression profiling showed that some PagPIP and PagTIP members were highly expressed in vascular tissues and exhibited changes in transcript abundance under nitrogen and drought treatments. Compared with wild-type plants, the 35S:PagPIP2;6A overexpression lines were shorter before treatment and exhibited higher leaf relative water content and lower malondialdehyde content after water withholding. This study systematically characterized the subgenomic distribution, evolutionary features and expression patterns of the PagAQP family in 84K poplar and identified candidate genes for further functional investigation.
items.authors: Zhu M, Wang K, Wang J, Sun K, Wang H, Li Y, Wang J, Zhu S.

items.title: Cytological observations of the epithem and the epithem-mesophyll interface in Arabidopsis hydathodes.
items.abstract: Hydathodes are specialized leaf tissues that mediate guttation, the release of liquid water droplets from vascular plants. They consist of xylem endings, water pores, and the epithem, a tissue of small cells located between the xylem endings and water pores. Although previous studies have provided anatomical descriptions and emerging molecular insights into Arabidopsis thaliana hydathodes, how epithem cells differ from surrounding cells and how the epithem interfaces with surrounding tissues remain incompletely understood. In this study, we examined the anatomy of A. thaliana hydathodes using complementary imaging approaches. Microfocus-X-ray computed tomography visualized the three-dimensional morphology of hydathodes protruding from the abaxial leaf surface. Light microscopy showed that the epithem consisted of densely packed cells with limited intercellular spaces. Quantitative analyses showed that the cross-sectional area of epithem cells was approximately 25-40% that of mesophyll cells, and that epithem cells exhibited lower plastid occupancy. We further characterized cells located along the epithem-mesophyll boundary, which we provisionally refer to as boundary-like cells based on their position. These cells were closely arranged with limited intercellular spaces, contrasting with the prominent intercellular spaces among surrounding mesophyll cells. Despite this organization, quantitative analyses indicated that boundary-like cells more closely resembled mesophyll cells than epithem cells. To examine whether proteins from different cellular compartments enter guttation fluid, we used transgenic plants expressing GFP targeted to the apoplast, cytosol, or ER lumen. GFP was detected in guttation droplets only from plants expressing apoplastic GFP. Together, these findings refine our understanding of the cellular anatomy of A. thaliana hydathodes and provide a reporter-based approach for examining the movement of apoplastic macromolecules into guttation fluid.
items.authors: Yagi H, Mihara I, Ikeda T, Sano R, Demura T, Hara-Nishimura I, Hara-Nishimura I, Shimada T, Ueda H.

items.title: Genome-Wide Splicing Landscapes Across Poplar Cultivars Reveal a GBF3-Mediated Post-Transcriptional Switch Modulating Monolignol Biosynthesis.
items.abstract: Black poplars (Populus deltoides, P. nigra, and their hybrids) represents economically and ecologically vital hardwood taxa characterised by rapid biomass accumulation, superior wood properties, and wide adaptability. However, the post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms orchestrating xylem development in these perennial trees remain poorly understood. Here, we systematically profiled transcriptome and alternative splicing (AS) dynamics in the developing xylem across five representative cultivars: P. euramericana 'Zhonglin46' (Pe1), P. euramericana 'Guariento' (Pe2), P. nigra 'N179' (Pn1), P. deltoides 'Danhong' (Pd1), and P. deltoides 'Nanyang' (Pd2). RNA-seq analysis of 20 independent xylem libraries revealed 9,981 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and 6,638 alternatively spliced genes across 10 pairwise comparisons. Functional enrichment indicated that transcriptional variations primarily coordinates cell wall biosynthesis and cytoskeleton organisation, whereas AS preferentially tunes nucleic acid binding and metabolic processes. Regulatory network modelling positioned key AS events upstream of core xylogenesis cascades. Crucially, we identified the G-box binding factor GBF3 as a master splicing-regulated hub during secondary vascular differentiation. An intron retention event in GBF3 yields a truncated isoform with aberrant subcellular localisation and abolished DNA-binding capacity, which impairs its transcriptional repression of key lignin biosynthetic genes (PAL2, CAD1, and CCoAOMT2). Collectively, these high-resolution transcriptional and post-transcriptional landscapes illuminate the regulatory architecture of wood formation and provide a valuable genomic resource for trait improvement in woody perennials.
items.authors: Ma B, Chen Z, Wang H, Jiang C, An Y, Chen N, Huang L, Lu M, Zhang J.

items.title: Class III chitinases in Medicago truncatula facilitate arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis with Rhizophagus intraradices.
items.abstract: Plant chitinases are important defense enzymes in plant-microbe interactions and also participate in nodule symbiosis between legumes and nitrogen-fixing rhizobia. However, the roles of chitinases in arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) symbiosis remain incompletely defined. In this study, we characterized two class III chitinase genes in the legume Medicago truncatula (ecotype R108), namely MtCHIT3e and MtCHIT3f. Heterologous expression in Nicotiana benthamiana confirmed hydrolytic activity toward colloidal chitin, a fluorogenic chitooligosaccharide substrate, chitooligosaccharides, and lipo-chitooligosaccharides. In M. truncatula roots inoculated with AM fungi, transcripts of the two genes were significantly upregulated. Analysis of M. truncatula hairy roots transformed with promoter-β-glucuronidase constructs indicated strong induction of MtCHIT3e and MtCHIT3f promoter activity in response to applied chitooligosaccharide and lipo-chitooligosaccharide signals. Furthermore, fluorescent protein fusions localized the chitinases predominantly to the apoplast of host cells during AM colonization. Tnt1 insertion mutants in the chitinase genes exhibited reduced AM colonization, whereas nodule formation induced by Sinorhizobium meliloti was unaffected. Together, these results support a role for class III chitinases in promoting AM symbiosis and provide genetic evidence that they are required for optimal root colonization by AM fungi.
items.authors: Zhang YR, Wang YF, Liu QY, Wen J, Mysore KS, Reinhardt D, Xie ZP, Staehelin C.

items.title: Genome-wide analysis of the annexin gene family in alfalfa ( Medicago sativa L.) and functional characterization of MsANN22 under drought stress
items.abstract: Annexins are a conserved family of calcium-dependent phospholipid-binding proteins that participate in diverse plant stress responses. However, the annexin gene family in Medicago sativa and the molecular mechanisms underlying annexin-mediated drought tolerance remain largely unexplored. In this study, 73 MsANN genes were identified in the alfalfa genome. Their phylogenetic relationships, synteny, conserved motifs, gene structures, and promoter cis-acting elements were systematically analyzed. Synteny analysis revealed 75 segmental/whole-genome duplication-associated gene pairs but no tandem duplications, indicating that large-scale duplication was the major driver of MsANN family expansion. The MsANN promoters contained ABA- and drought-responsive elements. Expression profiling identified MsANN22 as a strongly drought-responsive gene encoding a cytoplasm-localized protein. MsANN22 overexpression enhanced drought tolerance in both Arabidopsis thaliana and alfalfa: in Arabidopsis, MsANN22 overexpression promoted seed germination under osmotic stress, whereas in alfalfa it enhanced antioxidant capacity, with superoxide dismutase and peroxidase activities reaching 1.38- and 1.70-fold those of wild-type plants, respectively. Consistently, MsANN22 -overexpressing alfalfa accumulated approximately 20% less malondialdehyde and exhibited reduced H O and O • accumulation, as indicated by DAB and NBT staining. Yeast two-hybrid and luciferase complementation assays further supported physical interactions of MsANN22 with MsIAA and MsPR-10. These findings provide insight into the molecular mechanism by which MsANN22 mediates drought tolerance and offer a candidate gene for improving drought resistance in alfalfa.
items.authors: Xie, Q., guangzhi, j., Wang, J., he, h., du, p., li, h., Meng, Z., shao, q., li, h.

items.title: Spatial recovery and persistence of Pseudomonas chlororaphis M71 and Trichoderma atroviride SC1 in grapevine following stem injection.
items.abstract: Establishing biocontrol agents (BCAs) within grapevine tissues could provide a means of protecting internal plant compartments, but little is known about their spatial and temporal fate after vascular delivery or whether the graft union constrains their distribution. We compared the internal recovery of two biologically contrasting BCAs, the bacterium Pseudomonas chlororaphis M71 and the filamentous fungus Trichoderma atroviride SC1, following controlled stem injection into rooted and grafted grapevine plants. A xylem-mobile dye was used as a reference for immediate passive fluid transport, while viable microbial recovery was assessed over time and complemented by quantitative isolation and microscopy. At 48 h, the dye generally showed broader longitudinal distribution than either of the microorganisms. The two microorganisms displayed markedly different patterns. M71 persisted for up to 56 days, but remained predominantly associated with tissues close to the injection site. In contrast, SC1 was recovered from a broader range of tissues, including roots, and remained detectable for up to 56 days. In grafted plants, both microorganisms were recovered on both sides of the graft union, indicating that the graft interface was not an absolute barrier, although recovery depended on microbial identity and inoculation position. Green fluorescent protein-labeled M71 cells and SC1 hyphae were observed within xylem vessels, confirming internal localization and, for SC1, vegetative development after injection. These results show that, and how, both microbial biology and grafted-plant architecture influence the internal fate of injected BCAs in grapevine.IMPORTANCEBeneficial microorganisms established inside grapevine tissues could potentially protect from infections regarding internal tissues, but little is known about how such microorganisms distribute and persist inside grapevine after injection into the plant tissues. This study shows that two biocontrol agents (BCAs) with contrasting biological characteristics follow markedly different spatial and temporal patterns. Pseudomonas chlororaphis M71 persisted mainly near the site of introduction, whereas Trichoderma atroviride SC1 was recovered from a broader range of tissues and developed hyphae within xylem vessels. Importantly, the graft union was not an absolute barrier to microbial recovery. These findings provide a framework for selecting where and when BCAs should be introduced during grapevine propagation and highlight that vascular access, persistence, and broad within-plant establishment are distinct properties that should be considered when developing endophytic biocontrol strategies.
items.authors: Brussi G, Martini A, Ratti C, Puopolo G, Mugnai L, Pertot I.

items.title: Serial Cryosectioning for the Spatial Transcriptomics of Plant Tissues.
items.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables genome-wide gene expression profiling while preserving tissue architecture, making it a powerful approach for studying plant developmental transitions. However, preparing small and structurally complex plant tissues for spatial transcriptomics remains technically challenging because samples must be rapidly preserved, precisely oriented, serially sectioned, and accurately positioned within the limited capture area of the Visium slides. Here, we describe an optimized workflow for cryo-embedding, serial cryosectioning, section placement, and data analysis of small plant samples for 10x Genomics Visium spatial transcriptomics. Using maize seedling shoot apices as the target, this protocol includes preparation of custom molds for optimal cutting temperature embedding, rapid fresh sample embedding, serial cryosectioning, section-position marking for Visium HD workflows, and morphological quality assessment of replicate tissue slides before transcript capture. The associated data analysis workflow includes Space Ranger processing, Seurat-based normalization and Harmony integration, anatomical domain annotation, pseudobulk and developmental trend analyses, RNA velocity, pseudotime analysis, transcription factor network analysis, single-cell reference mapping, and 3D transcriptome reconstruction. This computational workflow was developed and tested using maize Visium V1 data, but not Visium HD data. This protocol was used to generate serial spatial transcriptomes of maize shoot apices and developing leaf primordia, enabling reconstruction of gene expression transitions from the shoot apical meristem to sequential leaf developmental stages. The approach is also applicable to other small plant tissues, including Arabidopsis first true leaves and Marchantia thalli. Key features • Optimized cryo-embedding and cryosectioning workflow for small plant tissues for 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics. • A streamlined computational workflow for serial-section processing, spatial-domain annotation, 3D reconstruction, and developmental trajectory analysis.
items.authors: Wu CC, Hsieh KT, Yu CP, Chen YH, Chou SJ, Wu TY, Ho CK, Wu SH, Lu MJ, Li WH.

items.title: BvCaM7 Participates in Sugar Beet (Beta vulgaris L.) Resistance to CLS (Cercospora Leaf Spot) by Activating BvPAL via BvMYB108 and Is Accompanied by Calcium Dynamics.
items.abstract: CLS (Cercospora leaf spot) is a major constraint in sugar beet (Beta vulgaris L.) cultivation, yet the functions of CaM/CML family members in CLS resistance are unclear. This study identified the CaM/CML family in sugar beet and focused on BvCaM7, which was significantly upregulated under CLS. Calcium measurements revealed differential calcium dynamics between resistant and susceptible varieties at late stages. Lignin staining revealed enhanced vascular lignification in resistant lines. Molecular interaction assays confirmed that BvCaM7 interacts with BvCNGC14 and BvMYB108. LUC assays confirmed that BvMYB108 activates the PAL promoter, and coexpression with BvCaM7 enhanced this effect. Transient overexpression of BvCaM7 or BvMYB108 in tobacco was associated with reduced lesion development following Cercospora beticola (C. beticola.) inoculation, although defence gene induction kinetics (PR2/3/4, PAL, COL, PDF1.2) differed: BvMYB108 peaked at 12 h, whereas BvCaM7 sustained expression until 24 h. Both overexpressions increased superoxide dismutase (SOD) and peroxidase (POD) activities, but decreased catalase (CAT) activity. In summary, BvCaM7 activates the PAL pathway via BvMYB108, enhancing lignin-related defence. Furthermore, the BvCaM7-BvCNGC14 interaction and concomitant calcium changes provide clues for the potential involvement of calcium signalling. However, its specific role requires further validation. This study provides candidate genes for breeding CLS-resistant sugar beet.
items.authors: He M, Lou H, Ding G, Zhao C.

items.title: Diffusible signals from Azospirillum brasilense promote rice growth and induce distinct gene expression changes in plant roots.
items.abstract: Plants form associations with diverse beneficial microbes, including arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi, rhizobia, and plant growth-promoting bacteria (PGPB). Research on legume-rhizobia symbiosis (LRS) and AM symbiosis has demonstrated that molecular communication between symbiotic partners is essential for initiating these interactions. Genetic and biochemical studies have further identified both plant and microbial signals, as well as host genetic pathways, that regulate these interactions. However, most studies on plant-PGPB interactions have focused on direct application of PGPB to plant roots, leaving the early signaling mechanisms underlying these interactions poorly understood. In this study, we report that diffusible signals from A. brasilense can promote rice growth without direct contact between bacteria and plant roots, 7 days post-treatment (dpt). Using RNA sequencing, we identified 2,516 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in rice roots in response to diffusible signals from A. brasilense at 1 dpt. We identified differential expression of genes involved in flavonoid synthesis, defense responses, receptor activity, transcription factors, and hormone pathways. Comparative transcriptomic analysis of rice roots with or without contact with A. brasilense revealed both shared and unique gene expression patterns. We observed upregulation of certain defense-response genes (PAL, chitinase, thionin), transcription factors (AP2/ERFs, MYBs, WRKYs, and GRAS), and hormone-related (auxin and ethylene) genes without bacterial contact, but downregulation or no differential expression of these genes upon bacterial contact. This pattern suggests that initial induction followed by subsequent suppression of these genes may be crucial for establishing the interaction with A. brasilense. Our transcriptomic analysis also suggests that flavonoids may be required throughout the interaction, whereas nitrate transporters appear to be involved at later stages and likely require contact between plant roots and bacteria. Collectively, our findings reveal that diffusible signals from A. brasilense can promote rice growth and induce distinct gene expression changes in plant roots. These results provide novel insights into the early phase of rice-A. brasilense interaction and highlight the potential for leveraging plant-PGPB signaling mechanisms to enhance crop growth under adverse environmental conditions.
items.authors: Hoggard S, Calhoun M, Bommes A, Rahmatallah Y, Neuhaus D, Glazko G, Mukherjee A.

items.title: The Stem of the Mediterranean Species Quercus ilex: a Forgotten Source of BVOCs.
items.abstract: Biogenic Volatile Organic Compounds (BVOCs) fulfil key ecological functions and have a significant impact on climate and air quality. However, research into BVOC fluxes from tree compartments other than the foliage remains limited and mainly restricted to conifers. In this study, we examined the stem emissions from Quercus ilex, an oak species that, despite lacking terpene storage pools, emits significant quantities of monoterpenes through its leaves. BVOC fluxes were measured using purpose-built dynamic stem chambers on four field-grown adult trees from spring to autumn. Q. ilex stems were found to be a net source of BVOCs, comprising mainly oxygenated and non-oxygenated monoterpenes and sesquiterpenes. Emissions fluctuated throughout the season with peak emissions in the summer. During summer months, the daily mean emission rate of monoterpenes ranged between 0.7 and 37 pmol·m-2·s-1stem surface (0.1 - 5.1 ng·m-2·s-1) whereas that of sesquiterpene ranged from 0.1 and 22 pmol·m-2·s-1 (0.02 - 4.5 ng·m-2·s-1) and even up to 95 pmol·m-2·s-1 (19 ng·m-2·s-1) for one of the trees. Deposition of BVOCs, primarily the major monoterpenes emitted by Q. ilex leaves and their secondary oxidation products, were occasionally observed but in minor quantities. Stem emissions were mainly driven by temperature with positive exponential relationships. Furthermore, they increased with lower predawn leaf water potential values, meaning with increasing drought stress, but they decreased with air humidity and stem transpiration. Significant emission differences were also observed between individual trees, possibly related to biotic stress. Overall, the results demonstrate that stems of non-coniferous trees such as oaks can be a net source of BVOCs, particularly of highly reactive terpenoids, which should be taken into account in emission inventories. Further research is needed to truly understand the mechanisms behind stem emissions, as well as their role in the forest ecosystem.
items.authors: Bihanic C, Thiriet A, Kempf J, Longepierre D, Limousin JM, Borbon A, Staudt M.

items.title: Carotenoid Cleavage Dioxygenase 8 Enhances Interspecific Facilitation in Maize-Soybean Intercropping via Arbuscular Mycorrhiza Symbiosis Under Phosphate Limitation.
items.abstract: Carotenoid Cleavage Dioxygenase 8 (CCD8) regulates strigolactone (SL) biosynthesis, which mediates the establishment of arbuscular mycorrhiza fungal (AMF) symbiosis. This symbiosis makes a major contribution in nutrient uptake, thereby improving crop productivity, mostly without the need for specific inoculation. Quantifying the extent of this contribution in typical intercropping systems remains challenging. A pot experiment was conducted using ZmCCD8 knockout (zmccd8), overexpression (ZmCCD8-OE), and wild type (WT) maize lines, grown in sole cropping or intercropping with soybean under low phosphate (LP) and control conditions. Intercropped ZmCCD8-OE and soybean showed a 61.9% higher overyielding effect, partially attributed to a 72.7% greater AMF colonisation rate in ZmCCD8-OE than WT counterparts under LP. Together with the greater root, AMF promoted P accumulation by 58% and 35% in the ZmCCD8-OE shoot and root, respectively. Conversely, intercropped zmccd8 conferred negative impacts under LP, corresponding to 47.6% and 63.4% less overyielding and AMF colonisation, respectively. Consistent with these results was differential expression of genes (CCD8, D14, CCaMK, CYCLOPS, RAM1, PT6/PT8) regulating AMF symbiosis and P uptake in maize and soybean. Collectively, ZmCCD8 enhances interspecific facilitation by stimulating root growth and AMF symbiosis, providing a genetic approach for higher crop productivity in intercropping systems without inoculation.
items.authors: Hassan MU, Zhong Y, Ishfaq M, Zhang C, Xu L, Li X.

items.title: Nanobubble-Driven Precision Aeration: Deciphering Abiotic Hypoxia Responses via Multi-Omics for Next-Generation Smart Agriculture.
items.abstract: Soil salinity and drought can restrict oxygen availability in the root zone, adding hypoxic stress to the ionic, osmotic, and hydraulic constraints experienced by crops. Nanobubble (NB) water offers a chemical-free approach for delivering highly dispersed oxygen and sustaining dissolved oxygen during irrigation. This review connects the physicochemical behavior of NBs with plant responses to salinity- and drought-associated hypoxia. It examines restoration of aerobic respiration and ATP homeostasis, modulation of ethylene response factor group VII and hypoxia-responsive gene signaling, recovery of ion transport and aquaporin function, redox regulation, hormonal cross-talk, and rhizosphere microbiome responses. Evidence from rice, maize, wheat, cotton, and controlled-environment systems is evaluated alongside opportunities for nanoparticle co-delivery, nanofertilizers, seed priming, and sensor-guided irrigation. The review also outlines how transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, epigenomics, ionomics, and phenomics can resolve NB-mediated mechanisms across the plant-soil continuum. Current evidence supports NB irrigation as a promising precision-aeration platform, but field-scale validation, standardized NB characterization, dose-response studies, energy and cost assessments, and long-term environmental safety analyses remain necessary before broad agricultural deployment.
items.authors: Kareem HA, Saleem S, Hafeez MB, Ahmad N, Yin DC.

items.title: Overexpression of SiLEA_2-6 from Saussurea involucrata Enhances Salt and Osmotic Tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana.
items.abstract: LEA_2 proteins are intrinsically disordered proteins implicated in plant abiotic stress tolerance; however, their functional characterization under salt and osmotic stress, particularly regarding stress-inducible peripheral redistribution, remains limited.
